svg.aria-label: How to write சரியா: 5 parts, ச, ர, ி, ய, ா, one after another
svg.title: Writing சரியா
svg.desc: 5 parts written one after another: ச, ர, ி, ய, ா (tamil). The parts are in the order the hand writes them, which is not always the order they are typed: a vowel sign written to the left of its consonant comes before it. Each vowel sign is drawn on its own, without the consonant it attaches to. Each part has its own group of frames; frame N of a group shows movements 1 to N of that part, the movement being added drawn in ink over the finished part, whose outline is read from _fonts/NotoSansTamil-Static.ttf. Each part is drawn at its own scale from its own cited stroke order, so the strip does not show how large the parts are next to each other, how far apart they sit, or any join between them. Stroke order: ச: Sankaran Radhakrishnan, Tamil Script Learners Manual, Appendix I: Hand-movements, Frame 3, ச (University of Texas at Austin), p. 191 <https://sites.la.utexas.edu/tamilscript/files/2009/08/hw_lettersinstructions.pdf>; ர: Sankaran Radhakrishnan, Tamil Script Learners Manual, Appendix I: Hand-movements, Frame 3, ர (University of Texas at Austin), p. 191 <https://sites.la.utexas.edu/tamilscript/files/2009/08/hw_lettersinstructions.pdf>; ி: HP Labs India, Lipi Toolkit, Lipi Indic Character Recognizers 4.0, Tamil recognizer, class 37 (ி, i sign): stored online-handwriting prototypes from native Tamil writers (MIT licence, 2012) <https://lipitk.sourceforge.net/lipi-reco.htm>; ய: Sankaran Radhakrishnan, Tamil Script Learners Manual, Appendix I: Hand-movements, Frame 1, ய (University of Texas at Austin), p. 190 <https://sites.la.utexas.edu/tamilscript/files/2009/08/hw_lettersinstructions.pdf>; ா: HP Labs India, Lipi Toolkit, Lipi Indic Character Recognizers 4.0, Tamil recognizer, class 36 (ா, aa sign): stored online-handwriting prototypes from native Tamil writers (MIT licence, 2012) <https://lipitk.sourceforge.net/lipi-reco.htm>. Source notes on variation: ச: Frame 3 numbers three upper-frame movements and a fourth that turns around ச's lower-left bowl. Native writers draw the four movements as one continuous stroke, and this ductus follows them in order without lifting: movement 3 ends at the tip of the middle bar, so the pen comes back along the bar to the inner crossing before it turns around the bowl. In HP Labs India's online Tamil handwriting data (the LipiTk 4.0 Tamil isolated-character recognizer, trained on hpl-tamil-iso-char), 88% of the 176 stored prototypes of ச are a single pen-down stroke. Tamil handwriting varies by school; this is one attested order fitted to the bundled Noto Sans Tamil outline. ர: Frame 3 identifies ர as the three-movement ஈ frame plus a slightly angular short fourth movement. Native writers draw the four movements as one continuous stroke, and this ductus follows them in order without lifting: the first movement runs down the left upright, so the pen climbs back up it to begin the top bar and returns along the bar to the central upright. In HP Labs India's online Tamil handwriting data (the LipiTk 4.0 Tamil isolated-character recognizer, trained on hpl-tamil-iso-char), 90% of the 189 stored prototypes of ர are a single pen-down stroke. Tamil handwriting varies by school; this is one attested order fitted to the bundled Noto Sans Tamil outline. ி: The recognizer stores native Tamil writers' tablet pen traces, each resampled to 60 points. 205 of the 206 stored prototypes of the i sign are one pen-down stroke. In 161 of those 205 the pen starts at the tip of the hook and first moves up; 200 turn clockwise, over the top to the right; 152 end at the foot of the stem. The traces are scaled to a square, so they fix the start, the direction and the pen lifts, not the proportions: the path is fitted to the bundled Noto Sans Tamil outline of the sign on its own. Handwriting varies by writer. ய: Frame 1 numbers six joined movements for ய: down the left, around its foot, up and back down the central upright, across the bottom, and up the right. Tamil handwriting varies by school; this is one attested continuous order fitted to the bundled Noto Sans Tamil outline. ா: The recognizer stores native Tamil writers' tablet pen traces, each resampled to 60 points. 189 of the 217 stored prototypes of the aa sign (87%) are one pen-down stroke. In 135 of those 189 the pen starts on the left, partway down, and first moves down; 154 end at the foot of the right upright. So the left upright is drawn down, climbed back to the top bar, and the right upright comes last, without lifting. The traces are scaled to a square, so they fix the start, the direction and the pen lifts, not the proportions: the path is fitted to the bundled Noto Sans Tamil outline, whose top bar runs a little past the right upright. Handwriting varies by writer.
svg.text: How it is written — 5 parts, one after another
Part 1 of 5 — one unbroken stroke · 4 movements
Part 2 of 5 — one unbroken stroke · 4 movements
Part 3 of 5 — one unbroken stroke · 3 movements
Part 4 of 5 — one unbroken stroke · 6 movements
Part 5 of 5 — one unbroken stroke · 3 movements
Part 1: stroke order after Sankaran Radhakrishnan, Tamil Script Learners Manual, Appendix I: Hand-movements, Frame 3, ச (University of Texas at Austin), p. 191
Part 2: stroke order after Sankaran Radhakrishnan, Tamil Script Learners Manual, Appendix I: Hand-movements, Frame 3, ர (University of Texas at Austin), p. 191
Part 3: stroke order after HP Labs India, Lipi Toolkit, Lipi Indic Character Recognizers 4.0, Tamil recognizer, class 37 (ி, i sign): stored online-handwriting prototypes from native
Part 4: stroke order after Sankaran Radhakrishnan, Tamil Script Learners Manual, Appendix I: Hand-movements, Frame 1, ய (University of Texas at Austin), p. 190
Part 5: stroke order after HP Labs India, Lipi Toolkit, Lipi Indic Character Recognizers 4.0, Tamil recognizer, class 36 (ா, aa sign): stored online-handwriting prototypes from
This order is attested, not standardised; the source records where it varies.
